requirements.title: 18-Page Graphic Novel Sample
requirements.definition: Produce an 18-page comic or graphic-novel script sample adapted from the supplied screenplay material and suitable for presentation to artists and potential crowdfunding backers.
requirements.boundary_note: The page count, selected story segment, and presentation purpose are attributes of one sample deliverable; panel-level formatting and editorial fidelity are independently assessable behaviors represented separately.

requirements.title: Panel-Based Sample Script Format
requirements.definition: Structure the sample as a professional comic script organized by pages and panels, with dialogue, captions, and visual direction while leaving precise balloon placement to the artist.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the structural representation of the sample, not its page count, story coverage, or the degree of permitted adaptation from the screenplay.

requirements.title: Creative Discretion in Sample Adaptation
requirements.definition: Allow the adapter to adjust pacing and presentation rather than reproduce the screenplay line-for-line, including converting scene description into voice-over captions and omitting minor exchanges when appropriate.
requirements.boundary_note: The permitted transformations are aspects of one editorial-discretion rule; this rule can change independently of the sample length and panel-based format.

requirements.title: Full-Length Graphic Novel Adaptation
requirements.definition: Create a prospective 96–102-page comic-script adaptation using the supplied scripts and novel, with the exact story coverage and narrative endpoint to be determined within the page limit.
requirements.boundary_note: This is separate from the completed sample because it is a distinct future deliverable that can be deferred independently. Page count, source selection, story coverage, and ending treatment are attributes of that one adaptation task rather than separate Requirements.

unresolved_candidates.description: The full-length adaptation is identifiable, but its authoritative source, exact story coverage, and self-contained-versus-cliffhanger ending remain unresolved values for later lifecycle annotation.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Today’s progress has been good: I’ve drafted a tentative breakdown that reaches Tom’s meeting with Apollonia on comic page 18. As I continue, I may find that this pace is too brisk if some beats require more room to breathe.

Before proceeding further, I want to check two questions—or, more accurately, two thoughts about the script—with you:

1.. In several places, I may adapt portions of the scene descriptions into "voice over" caption text.

2\. To use the available page space efficiently, I may omit a few brief exchanges. One example is at the bottom of page 41, where Carter tells Tom that he is invited to the dinner shown in the following scene.

Would deviations of this size be acceptable, or should the comic reproduce the screenplay line-for-line? Let me know what you think.

Thanks.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Using what I had already written, I worked through the numbers.

First, could you clarify whether the request is for 102 pages of screenplay or 102 pages of comic? My completed work produced an approximate screenplay-to-comic conversion of roughly 3:1.

If part 4 is approximately the same length as episode 1, then parts 1 through 4 should amount to around 54-60 comic pages. I could complete that scope for $625 with a turnaround of 5 weeks. If I can reuse 18 pages from the sample script with only light revision and page reflowing, I could reduce that price to $475.

The larger option of 96-102 comic pages is also possible, but it would require covering more of the story, presumably through episode 5 or 6. For that scope, I propose $1125 with a 7-week turnaround. With 18 pages of the sample script reused, the price would instead be $950.

Please let me know which option is closer to what you have in mind and whether these terms work for you.

Thanks,
Dom

source_message.text:
Thank you very much. At that rate, I can devote more time to finding the best way to present everything instead of adhering so closely to the screenplay.

Should I begin in three weeks, or wait until you explicitly say "go?"

I can commit to scripting 96-102 comic pages. After reviewing the next five episodes and the novel, I’ll determine how much of the story fits within that space. While doing so, should I pace the adaptation with the eventual remainder of the story in mind? In other words, should this section feel self-contained, or should it leave readers asking, "What’s next?"

Thanks,
Dom
